AUTHOR: Villon
TITLE: A new method to control error rates in automated species identification with deep learning algorithms
SPECIES: 20 coral reef fish species (e.g., Naso brevirostris, Zanclus cornutus, Chromis ternatensis)
DATA: Own GoPro HD videos (175 videos, 83 h) from Mayotte; cropped single-fish images: T0 train (130 videos), T1 threshold-tuning (20 videos), T2 test (25 videos)
V_EV: Methods, Data: 'The videos were recorded between 2 and 30 m deep, with a broad range of luminosity, transparency, and benthic environment conditions'
D2: T0 130 videos (69,169 imgs) / T1 20 videos (6,320) / T2 25 videos (13,232)
D_EV: Methods, Data: 'two independent datasets made of different videos recorded on different days and on different sites than videos used to build the training dataset.'
R_EV: Methods, Data: 'We used 3 independent fish images datasets from the Mayotte Island (Western Indian Ocean) to train and test our CNN model'
C_EV: Fig. 5: 'Average distribution of correct, wrong, and unsure classifications for all species along a gradient of confidence threshold score.'
E_EV: Results: 'The mean rate of correct classification of fish images inT2 by the raw CNN was of 78.0%' (classification rates/accuracy only)
ARCH: ResNet (100-layer, TensorFlow) classifier + species-specific softmax thresholds with 'unsure' class
NOTE: Classification of pre-cropped single-fish images; reports per-class thresholds and an 'unsure' reject class so normal C rules applied (C1=Y, C4=Y, threshold gradient Fig. 5 -> C_ALL=P). Paper explicitly contrasts its method with calibration (temperature scaling etc.) but does not compute ECE/reliability -> C2=없음; threshold-based reject not coded as C3. Test videos from different days and sites but same Mayotte campaign -> D credit only (P2), R1=N. D1 coded 영상(video) (also different sites/days). D4=Y: authors state design 'ensures that our results are not biased by similar acquisition conditions'. Visibility ('transparency', 'luminosity') qualitative only; depth 2-30 m. Camera platform (diver vs fixed) not stated.
